lessons.title: Premiers mots d'auteur
lessons.oneGoal: Students discover what an author does using simple French words

opening.activity: Show pictures of authors writing. Use gestures: point to self 'Je suis...', point to book 'livre', make writing motion 'auteur écrit'.

main.activity: Look at familiar books and find author names. Students practice saying 'auteur' while pointing to author name. Play 'author actions' - pretend to write, think, read.

closing.activity: Circle time: Each student says 'auteur' and makes writing gesture. Show tomorrow we'll think of our own ideas.

lessons.troubleshooting: If vocabulary is too hard, just use 'livre' and gestures for writing
lessons.realWorldConnection: Authors write the books we read every day - just like the ones in our classroom

lessons.title: Mes idées spéciales
lessons.oneGoal: Students share one idea they could write about

opening.activity: Review: 'Hier, nous avons parlé d'auteur.' Point to head 'idée', make thinking gesture. 'Auteurs ont des idées.'

main.activity: Show picture prompts (family, pets, toys, food). Students point to what gives them ideas. Use thought bubbles - students hold bubble and share one idea through pictures or words.

closing.activity: Put ideas in 'idea jar' (pictures or words). 'Demain, nous dessinerons nos idées.'

lessons.troubleshooting: If no ideas come, start with 'Qu'est-ce que tu aimes?' and accept any response
lessons.realWorldConnection: Everyone has special ideas worth sharing - just like when we tell family about our day

lessons.title: Dessiner mes histoires
lessons.oneGoal: Students draw pictures to show their story ideas

opening.activity: Review yesterday's ideas from jar. Model: take idea, say 'Je vais dessiner', draw simple picture while talking.

main.activity: Students choose their idea and draw. Teacher circulates: 'Qu'est-ce que tu dessines?' Encourage details through questions and gestures.

closing.activity: Gallery walk - students hold pictures and walk around to see others. Simple comments: 'J'aime ton image.'

lessons.troubleshooting: If perfectionism blocks drawing, model 'good enough' drawing yourself
lessons.realWorldConnection: Pictures help us tell stories when words are hard - like when we draw for family

lessons.title: Mots simples, grandes histoires
lessons.oneGoal: Students use 2-3 French words to describe their drawings

opening.activity: Look at yesterday's drawings together. Model: show drawing, say 2-3 simple words 'chat, maison, content'.

main.activity: Students practice saying 2-3 French words about their picture with partner. Teacher provides word cards as supports. Record some students if they want.

closing.activity: Few volunteers share their words with class. Celebrate effort over perfection.

lessons.troubleshooting: If students are silent, let them point to word cards instead of speaking
lessons.realWorldConnection: We use words to help others understand our pictures - like when we explain our drawings to family

lessons.title: Écouter les histoires
lessons.oneGoal: Students listen to simple French stories and identify key elements

opening.activity: Review: 'Nous avons créé nos images et mots.' Today: 'Écouter d'autres auteurs.' Put on 'listening ears' (hands cupped to ears).

main.activity: Read simple French story with lots of pictures and gestures. Stop to ask 'Qui?' (character), 'Où?' (place), 'Quoi?' (action). Students respond with gestures or simple words.

closing.activity: Students use story element cards to show what they heard. Simple sharing in circle.

lessons.troubleshooting: If story is too complex, just focus on pictures and ask 'Qu'est-ce que tu vois?'
lessons.realWorldConnection: We learn by listening to stories around us - just like when family tells us stories

lessons.title: Personnages amusants
lessons.oneGoal: Students create and name a simple character

opening.activity: Review yesterday's story characters. 'Qui était dans l'histoire?' Show character cards from story.

main.activity: Students create their own character - draw or use template. Give character a name (French or English OK). Practice introducing character: 'Voici [name]'.

closing.activity: Character parade - students introduce their characters to the class. Quick and fun, no pressure.

lessons.troubleshooting: If students are stuck on names, let them use their own name or favorite toy's name
lessons.realWorldConnection: Stories need characters just like our lives have people - family, friends, pets

lessons.title: Où se passe l'histoire?
lessons.oneGoal: Students choose and describe a simple setting

opening.activity: Bring back characters from yesterday. 'Où habite ton personnage?' Show place cards (maison, école, parc).

main.activity: Students choose a place for their character and draw simple background. Practice saying where character lives: '[Name] habite [lieu]'.

closing.activity: Students place character in their setting and share with partner. Simple presentations if time allows.

lessons.troubleshooting: If students get frustrated with drawing, use place cards they can choose and point to
lessons.realWorldConnection: Everything happens somewhere - stories need places too, just like where we live and play

lessons.title: Que fait mon personnage?
lessons.oneGoal: Students plan one simple action for their character

opening.activity: Review: character and place. Now 'Que fait [character name]?' Model actions with gestures.

main.activity: Students choose one action for their character (courir, manger, jouer). Act out the action, then add it to their character story.

closing.activity: Action circle - students say their character's name and action, class repeats the action together.

lessons.troubleshooting: If students can't think of actions, start with basic ones they know: walk, eat, sleep
lessons.realWorldConnection: People do things - our characters should too, just like how we do different activities all day

lessons.title: Première page d'auteur
lessons.oneGoal: Students create their first story page with picture and one sentence

opening.activity: Review all elements: character, setting, action. 'Maintenant, nous créons notre première page d'histoire!'

main.activity: Students combine their character, setting, and action into one page. Draw picture and write/copy one simple sentence with support.

closing.activity: Students admire their first story page. Celebrate: 'Vous êtes des auteurs!' Save pages carefully for tomorrow.

lessons.troubleshooting: If perfectionism stops progress, remind students that first drafts don't need to be perfect
lessons.realWorldConnection: Every book starts with the first page - just like how we start anything new step by step

lessons.title: Partager avec la classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students show their page and read their sentence to a partner

opening.activity: Bring out story pages. 'Hier, nous avons créé nos premières pages. Aujourd'hui, nous partageons avec nos amis.'

main.activity: Partner sharing - students take turns showing their page and reading/telling their sentence. Switch partners halfway through.

closing.activity: Circle sharing - few volunteers share with whole class. Focus on celebration and encouragement.

lessons.troubleshooting: If students are too nervous to share, let them just show their picture without words
lessons.realWorldConnection: Authors share their work so others can enjoy it - just like when we show family our artwork

lessons.title: Améliorer mon histoire
lessons.oneGoal: Students add one detail to make their story better

opening.activity: Look at story pages together. 'Comment pouvons-nous améliorer nos histoires?' Show examples of adding details.

main.activity: Students choose one detail to add - color words, feeling words, or size words. Add to picture or sentence with support.

closing.activity: Compare before and after pages. Celebrate improvements: 'Regardez comme c'est mieux!'

lessons.troubleshooting: If students are resistant to changes, frame it as 'adding' rather than 'fixing'
lessons.realWorldConnection: We can always make our work a little better - just like when we tidy our room or improve our bike riding

lessons.title: Deuxième page magique
lessons.oneGoal: Students create a second page continuing their story

opening.activity: Review first pages. 'Que se passe-t-il après?' Model continuing a story with simple transition.

main.activity: Students create second page showing what happens next in their story. Support with 'Et puis...' or 'Après...' starters.

closing.activity: Students put pages together and see their two-page story. Celebrate growth: 'Vous avez écrit une histoire de deux pages!'

lessons.troubleshooting: If continuing is too hard, let students create a second scene with same character in different activity
lessons.realWorldConnection: Stories continue - there's always more to tell, just like our day has many different parts

lessons.title: Chaise d'auteur spéciale
lessons.oneGoal: Students sit in the author's chair and read their story to the class

opening.activity: Introduce the special author's chair. 'Cette chaise est pour les vrais auteurs. Vous êtes des auteurs!'

main.activity: Each student takes turn in author's chair reading their two-page story. Class gives positive comments using simple phrases.

closing.activity: Group celebration. Students say what they liked about being authors. Take photo of each student in author's chair.

lessons.troubleshooting: If students freeze up, let them just show their pictures and tell one thing about their story
lessons.realWorldConnection: Authors share their finished work with audiences - just like when musicians perform or artists show paintings

lessons.title: Mon livre fini
lessons.oneGoal: Students complete their mini-book and add a cover

opening.activity: Show real books with covers. 'Tous les livres ont une couverture. Nous créons nos couvertures aujourd'hui.'

main.activity: Students create cover with title and illustration. Staple pages together to make complete book. Practice being proud of their creation.

closing.activity: Book parade - students walk around showing completed books. Add books to classroom library with special 'authored by' labels.

lessons.troubleshooting: If perfectionism delays completion, remind students that published authors also revise after first books
lessons.realWorldConnection: Finished books have covers and titles like real books - now their book can sit with other books on the shelf

lessons.title: Nouvelle aventure créative
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore different story types through play

opening.activity: Review completed books. 'Maintenant, explorons différents types d'histoires!' Show examples: funny, scary, adventure.

main.activity: Students experiment with different story types through drawing and play. No pressure to complete, just explore creativity.

closing.activity: Share discoveries: 'Quel type d'histoire préférez-vous?' Light discussion about different story preferences.

lessons.troubleshooting: If students can't think of new ideas, let them modify their original character into new situation
lessons.realWorldConnection: There are many different types of stories to create - just like there are different types of games and activities

lessons.title: Illustrateur professionnel
lessons.oneGoal: Students focus on creating detailed illustrations for stories

opening.activity: Look at detailed illustrations in picture books. 'Certaines personnes sont illustrateurs - ils créent les images pour les livres.'

main.activity: Students create detailed illustrations focusing on artistic technique. Encourage attention to details, colors, backgrounds.

closing.activity: Art gallery walk - students display illustrations and admire each other's artistic work with positive comments.

lessons.troubleshooting: If students are afraid to 'mess up' good paper, remind them that artists make many drafts
lessons.realWorldConnection: Some people specialize in making pictures for books - their art helps stories come alive

lessons.title: Histoires ensemble
lessons.oneGoal: Students collaborate to create a group story

opening.activity: Discuss working together: 'Parfois, les auteurs travaillent ensemble.' Model how to share ideas respectfully.

main.activity: Small groups (3-4 students) create one story together. Each student contributes one element. Practice compromise and sharing ideas.

closing.activity: Groups share their collaborative stories. Celebrate teamwork and different perspectives in one story.

lessons.troubleshooting: If collaboration is too challenging, let students work in pairs instead of larger groups
lessons.realWorldConnection: Sometimes authors work together to create stories - just like how families work together on projects

lessons.title: Bibliothèque de classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students organize their books into a class library

opening.activity: Look at all the books students have created. 'Regardez tous ces livres! Nous avons une bibliothèque d'auteurs!'

main.activity: Students help organize their books into class library. Create categories, make labels, set up checkout system for reading each other's books.

closing.activity: Admire the completed class library. Students choose one book written by classmate to 'check out' for reading.

lessons.troubleshooting: If students are protective of their books, start with just displaying them before implementing checkout
lessons.realWorldConnection: Libraries collect books so everyone can read them - now classmates can enjoy each other's stories

lessons.title: Lire aux petits
lessons.oneGoal: Students practice reading their books to younger students

opening.activity: Discuss being 'big kids' who can teach. 'Vous pouvez partager vos histoires avec les petits enfants.'

main.activity: Students practice reading their books aloud with expression. If possible, visit kindergarten class to share stories, or practice with stuffed animals.

closing.activity: Reflect on being teachers and authors. Discuss how it feels to share stories with others.

lessons.troubleshooting: If reading aloud is too challenging, let students just show pictures and tell story in simple words
lessons.realWorldConnection: Older students can share stories with younger ones - just like how family members read to each other

lessons.title: Célébration d'auteurs
lessons.oneGoal: Students celebrate their growth as young French authors

opening.activity: Look back at journey from Lesson 1 to now. 'Regardez comme vous avez grandi comme auteurs!'

main.activity: Celebration party with sharing of favorite parts of being authors. Present author certificates. Create memory book of writing journey.

closing.activity: Final circle: each student completes 'Je suis un auteur parce que...' Group picture with all their books.

lessons.troubleshooting: If some students feel their work isn't good enough, emphasize effort and growth over perfection
lessons.realWorldConnection: Authors celebrate when they finish their work - just like any accomplishment deserves recognition
